---
title: "Submission Criteria"
subtitle: "Find out what we value in a submission!"
---

The Methods Hub publishes resources that

1. fall within the **scope** of the social sciences and are relevant to them,
2. follow the principles of **open** science, and
3. meet standards of **quality** and accessibility.

If your method or tutorial meets these criteria, submit it for review on the [Methods Hub Portal](https://methodshub.gesis.org). Every submission is checked for compliance with the criteria before publication. Each criterion is described in more detail below.

Additionally, we place a high value on **interactive** submissions! What does this mean? To ensure an exploratory user experience, we prefer methods and tutorials that include interactive elements, where users can modify one or more parameters and see how their changes affect the script's behavior. For this, we integrate so-called **interactive environments**. -> Learn here how to get the most out of your submission!

## Scope

- The method or tutorial is relevant for the social sciences.
- The method or tutorial belongs to a relevant task of the [Methods Hub Tasks Taxonomy](https://methodshub.gesis.org/submit/taxonomy/). If it does not fit into our taxonomy, contact us at [methodshub@gesis.org](mailto:methodshub@gesis.org).

## Openness

- The method or tutorial is developed in an open-source programming language (e.g., Python or R).
- The method or tutorial is publicly accessible in a Git repository.
- For methods: the Git repository contains one and only one method.
- The method or tutorial is [published under an open license](https://opensource.guide/legal/#which-open-source-license-is-appropriate-for-my-project).

## Quality

This section outlines documentation and code quality criteria.

[TODO: add more relating to interactive env?]

### Documentation quality

These files **must** be in your Git repository before you submit.

**The content file.** Your repository needs a file containing the content that is rendered on the Methods Hub page. It should follow the structure of our templates.

- **Methods:** a [Methods Hub–friendly README](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/method/template.md?plain=1) (can be `README.md` or another file).
- **Tutorials:** the tutorial itself, in one of the accepted formats:
  - [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) (`.qmd`) – see the template [`tutorial/template.qmd`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/tutorial/template.qmd)
  - [Jupyter Notebook](https://nbformat.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html) (`.ipynb`) – see the template [`tutorial/template.ipynb`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/tutorial/template.ipynb). Jupyter Notebooks are limited to a single programming language.
  - [R Markdown](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/) (`.Rmd`) – if possible, port it to Quarto.
  - [Pandoc Markdown](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#pandocs-markdown) (`.md`)

**A Binder environment.** Your repository contains the files needed to set up a [Binder environment](https://mybinder.readthedocs.io/en/latest/examples/sample_repos.html#managing-languages) for the Methods Hub. These configuration files can be at the root level or in a directory named `.binder` or `binder`.

- A configuration file for installing all requirements, e.g., [`requirements.txt`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/binder-examples/python/requirements.txt) for Python, [`install.R`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/binder-examples/r/install.R) for R, or [`environment.yml`](https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/YOUR-REPO/blob/main/binder-examples/conda/environment.yml) for conda and other languages. We recommend pinning dependency versions.
- The [`postBuild`](https://methodshub.gesis.org/snippet/postBuild) file that installs Quarto.
- The Binder environment builds without errors.

**License and citation.**

- A `LICENSE` file with an [open license](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/adding-a-license-to-a-repository) at the root level.
- A [`CITATION.cff`](https://citation-file-format.github.io/) file at the root level.

**Reproducibility.** All examples can be reproduced with reasonable accuracy using only publicly available resources.

### Code quality

- The method code contains documentation (comments) for parameters and decisions, so that others can adjust the method.
- The method code is structured into modules (where needed).

::: {.callout-note}
## Exemption for peer-reviewed software
The code quality criteria can be skipped for methods with a paper published in one of the following trusted third-party review venues:

- [Journal of Open Source Software](https://joss.theoj.org/)
- [The R Journal](https://journal.r-project.org/)
- [rOpenSci](https://ropensci.org/)

You can suggest further venues by email to the [Methods Hub team](mailto:methodshub@gesis.org).
:::
